theme: Airbnb calendar / availability / blocked-night datasets and occupancy-estimation code (San Francisco model, review-to-booking ratios)

candidates.name: ubdc-airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Containerized Django/Celery/PostgreSQL-PostGIS application (Python, Poetry, Docker) built by University of Glasgow's Urban Big Data Centre to continuously scrape Airbnb for user-defined geographic areas: new-listing discovery, listing detail harvesting, and calendar/availability harvesting. Has been run daily since 2020 to build a raw scraped archive (30 Scottish Travel-to-Work Areas + 10 UK locations from Jun 2021; the resulting derived dataset is restricted to UBDC staff, but the scraping code itself is public, 58 commits). Underpins the peer-reviewed method in Wang et al., 'Enhancing our understanding of short-term rental activity: A daily scrape-based approach for Airbnb listings' (PLOS ONE 2024, PMC10849255) which estimates occupancy/cancellations from calendar deltas rather than the review-rate (San Francisco) model.
candidates.why_useful: Directly addresses gap #2 (realised occupancy for STRs) and #17 (methods) with a working, non-review-based occupancy/cancellation-estimation pipeline (calendar-diff method) that is an alternative to the Inside Airbnb San Francisco model already in use; also relevant to gap #3 (booking lead time / cancellation, RNPL thesis) since the companion paper explicitly studies cancellation trends via calendar tracking.
candidates.license: repo contains a LICENCE.txt (type not confirmed by fetch)
candidates.last_activity: 58 commits; scraping documented as ongoing 2020-2025 per associated dataset record
candidates.time_coverage: code usable to scrape any date range going forward; documented runs 2020-2023+
candidates.size_hint: code repo only; underlying raw data (not on GitHub) spans 30+ months of daily calendars

candidates.name: Airbnb-Processing-Daily-Booking-Calendars
candidates.what_it_holds: Companion repo to the UBDC PLOS ONE paper: a 5-step Python pipeline (stp1-stp5) that turns consecutive daily Airbnb calendar scrapes into booking/cancellation events, focused on 'cancellation trend in Edinburgh during first lockdown'; includes a committed AggregatedFigures.xlsx with the paper's summary statistics.
candidates.why_useful: A concrete, working method for converting raw calendar snapshots into occupancy AND cancellation-rate time series — usable on our own Inside Airbnb calendar vintages to build a non-review-based occupancy estimator, and directly on-topic for the RNPL/cancellation thesis (gap #3).

candidates.name: Airbnb raw scraped data collection (UBDC)
candidates.what_it_holds: External (non-GitHub, university data repository) archive: daily-scraped Airbnb property characteristics, booking-calendar updates, booking policies, host info and reviews for 30 Scottish Travel-to-Work Areas + 10 UK locations, June 2021-Dec 2023 monthly-aggregated occupancy/visitor/income estimates at MSOA/Intermediate Zone level, DOI 10.5525/gla.researchdata.2056. Access restricted to UBDC staff for non-commercial academic use (not freely downloadable), but methodology and code (see ubdc-airbnb above) are open.
candidates.why_useful: Even though the raw store itself is gated, it documents exactly what a daily-calendar-scrape occupancy product looks like at scale (fields, geography, cadence) and is the dataset behind the peer-reviewed alternative to the San Francisco review-rate model — useful as a specification to replicate on our own calendars.
candidates.size_hint: not disclosed; monthly small-area summaries + full daily calendars held internally

candidates.name: Airbnb daily listings/calendars (UBDC)
candidates.what_it_holds: Related UBDC data-repository record for daily Airbnb listings/calendars (companion/earlier record to 2056); same daily-scrape lineage.
candidates.why_useful: Second UBDC data record worth checking for looser access terms or a different (possibly earlier/broader) date range than 2056.
candidates.license: unknown, likely same restricted terms as 2056

candidates.name: airbnb-data-collection (Tom Slee)
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python/PostgreSQL scraper for Airbnb listings (the predecessor project to Inside Airbnb, run 2014-2017). No data files committed to the repo itself; historical CSV extracts (2014-2016 vintages, pre-dating Inside Airbnb's own coverage) are hosted externally on the author's site tomslee.net/airbnb-data-collection-get-the-data. Inactive since 2019 (author states no longer maintained), 250 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #1 (historical/archived Airbnb dumps pre-2023): this is the oldest known systematic Airbnb listings archive (2014-2016), predating Inside Airbnb, and could plug part of the pre-2023 hole even though it lacks calendar/availability fields (listings + review counts only, useful for review-rate occupancy proxies back to 2014).
candidates.last_activity: inactive since ~2019 (2017 final data collection per author announcement)
candidates.geography: multiple cities globally (city list configurable; exact historical coverage undocumented in repo)
candidates.size_hint: code only in repo; external CSV data volume undocumented

candidates.name: pyairbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python client for Airbnb's unofficial API (search by location, listing details, user info, map visualization); does not explicitly document calendar/availability endpoints in its README, and ships no committed dataset — queries Airbnb live. 19 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made client-side hook into Airbnb's own (undocumented) API surface, which is what a calendar/availability puller would build on; flagged as a scraper of airbnb.com itself, which per repo rules is a terms-of-service call for a human, not to be run.

candidates.name: airdna (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Third-party documentation/profile (by API Evangelist, not AirDNA itself) of the AirDNA Enterprise API surface: describes endpoints for market metrics, STR listing data, comparable-property sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates, occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, booking lead time and length of stay across AirDNA's 120,000+ tracked markets. No committed data, no working client, and the underlying API requires a paid AirDNA key.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms what fields a paid AirDNA export would carry (occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, booking lead time) which matches gap #2/#3 targets, but this repo itself is only a documentation mirror with no data or free access route.

candidates.name: AirBnB_Occupancy
candidates.what_it_holds: Implements a review-to-booking occupancy estimator in the style of the Inside Airbnb 'San Francisco model': assumes a 50% review-to-booking conversion rate, a per-city average length-of-stay parameter, and caps modeled occupancy (project notes discuss both a 70%-cap and a 0.95-cap variant); proposes an alternate calendar-based method that filters for hosts with 20+ listings renting 365+ days/year to separate 'confidently booked' from 'confidently available' listings as a calibration check on the review-based estimate.
candidates.why_useful: A clean, inspectable open-source reimplementation of the exact review-rate occupancy methodology already used by Inside Airbnb (which we already lean on) plus an independent calendar-based cross-check idea for calibrating that ratio — useful for validating/adjusting our own occupancy assumptions (gap #2).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: reimplements Inside Airbnb's own San Francisco model, which we already use; value is the independent calendar-based calibration idea, not new data

candidates.name: vrbo-calendar-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python (mechanize-based) scraper that pulls a single VRBO listing's calendar and returns a list of available dates. No committed dataset, no bulk-market capability as-is, minimal/no recent maintenance signal.
candidates.why_useful: Points at a feasible route to VRBO/HomeAway (Expedia Group) calendar availability, which would be a genuinely new competitor-supply data source (gap #9) not covered by anything we currently hold — but it is a single-listing tool that would need to be built out into a market-level crawler, and scraping vrbo.com is the same terms-of-service question as scraping airbnb.com.

candidates.name: check_availability
candidates.what_it_holds: Companion script to vrbo-calendar-scraper (same author) that checks availability across a list of VRBO calendar URLs. No committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Same rationale as vrbo-calendar-scraper: a starting point for VRBO availability tooling (gap #9), not itself a dataset.

candidates.name: kraina/airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Hugging Face dataset (not GitHub-native, external host) of Airbnb listings across 10 European cities, published as supplementary material for a research article on Airbnb pricing in Europe; includes standard Inside-Airbnb-style listing fields.
candidates.why_useful: Possible additional/older European-city cross-section beyond our current 13-city panel, worth a size/date check, but appears to be a single cross-sectional snapshot rather than a calendar/occupancy time series.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: likely overlaps our existing Inside Airbnb European-city coverage (Paris, London, Barcelona, Rome already held)

notes: Best find of the sweep is the UBDC (University of Glasgow) daily-calendar-scrape lineage: ubdc-airbnb (open scraper code), the YangWang-Glasgow processing pipeline (open code + a small results file), the underlying PLOS ONE 2024 paper (Wang et al., PMC10849255), and the restricted-access data records at researchdata.gla.ac.uk/2056 and /1904 -- together this is a full worked alternative to the Inside Airbnb 'San Francisco model' that estimates occupancy and CANCELLATIONS from consecutive daily calendar diffs rather than from review counts, which is exactly the RNPL/cancellation-rate gap (#3) as well as gap #2. The code is runnable against our own Inside Airbnb calendar vintages without touching airbnb.com at all (no new scraping needed) since it only requires two calendar snapshots to diff -- worth flagging to whoever owns the occupancy/RNPL workstream. Dead ends: most GitHub search results for 'airbnb occupancy' keyword combinations return the same handful of one-off student ML-price-prediction notebooks on the single Kaggle NYC/Seattle/Boston files (aarushi-vermaa, Sharayu26, tule2236, etc.) which were excluded per instructions as re-analyses of well-known files with nothing new; AirDNA/paid-API GitHub hits are documentation-only, no free data; VRBO/HomeAway calendar scrapers exist but are single-listing toy scripts, not market-level datasets, and scraping vrbo.com raises the same ToS issue as airbnb.com. Did not find any GitHub-hosted historical (pre-2023) Inside-Airbnb calendar mirror beyond Tom Slee's much older (2014-17, no-calendar) listings archive -- gap #1 (NYC 2023-06 to 2024-03, pre-2023 generally) still appears genuinely open on GitHub specifically; worth another scout checking Zenodo/Kaggle/archive.org directly rather than GitHub. Suggest a future scout specifically target the UBDC PLOS ONE paper's citation graph and Wang/Glasgow group's other repos for more calendar-diff occupancy code.
